uncited: Incremental Minimum Step Relaxed Sphere Tracing is a ray marching algorithm that accelerates traversal through empty space by combining the step-scaling logic of [Relaxed Sphere Tracing](9463-relaxed-sphere-tracing.md) with an incrementally increasing minimum step size.

It solves the performance bottleneck of standard sphere tracing in large empty volumes by allowing the step size to grow as the ray travels further from the origin, while retaining the safety checks of relaxed sphere tracing to prevent skipping intersections.
It is distinguished from basic sphere tracing by its adaptive step growth and from standard relaxed sphere tracing by the explicit addition of a growing minimum step component.
The method advances a ray along a parameter $t$ using a Signed Distance Function (SDF) to determine step sizes.
It maintains a minimum step size $msp$ that increases linearly with each iteration, ensuring that steps do not shrink below a growing threshold.
It also implements a backward correction mechanism to handle cases where the distance estimate drops significantly, which can occur with glassy artifacts or rapid changes in geometry.
